title: Martin D-21 Value Guide: 1955 To 1969
description: Vintage Martin D-21 values by production period, with concise notes on condition, originality and rosewood identification.
lede: Vintage Martin D-21 values generally range from $6,700 to $11,550 for 1960s guitars and $10,100 to $12,750 for 1956 to 1959 examples. Condition, originality and wood determine where a guitar falls within its range.
scope: Original D-21 production through 1969. Later D-21 Special and Custom Shop guitars need separate comparisons.
priceIntro: Estimated retail values in U.S. dollars, as of October 2026. Condition and originality affect the final value.

sections.heading: Condition And Originality
sections.html: Original finish, bridge, bridge plate and tuners affect value. Neck resets and repaired cracks need to be assessed by the quality and extent of the work. Confirm the back and sides on late-1969 guitars before using the Brazilian-rosewood range.

priceFootnote: The range depends on condition and originality. Dealer purchase offers and consignment proceeds differ from retail value.

title: Martin D-35 And D-35S Value Guide
description: Retail value ranges for Brazilian-rosewood Martin D-35 and D-35S guitars, with condition and wood distinctions.
lede: Brazilian-rosewood Martin D-35 values range from about $8,000 to $10,700. A 1966 to 1969 D-35S is approximately $8,800 to $13,200 in excellent original condition.
scope: Original 1960s D-35 and six-string D-35S. D12-35 twelve-strings have their own value guide.
priceIntro: Estimated retail values in U.S. dollars, as of October 2026. Condition and originality affect the final value.

sections.heading: Condition And Originality
sections.html: The D-35S is a 12-fret six-string guitar. Confirm all three back panels and both sides before using an all-Brazilian value. Refinishing, replacement bridge plates, neck work and extensive crack repairs can lower the value. Mixed-wood and heavily repaired guitars need individual appraisal.

priceFootnote: Ranges generally assume excellent original condition unless a row states otherwise. Dealer purchase offers and consignment proceeds differ from retail value.

title: Martin D-28 And D-28S Value Guide
description: Martin D-28 and D-28S retail value ranges by construction era, from prewar herringbones to 1960s Brazilian-rosewood guitars.
lede: Vintage Martin D-28 values vary sharply by construction period. Typical retail ranges are $12,000 to $20,000 for 1950s guitars and $6,000 to $12,000 for 1960s Brazilian-rosewood examples. Original prewar guitars can be worth substantially more.
scope: Original D-28s and D-28S guitars through 1969, with Brazilian rosewood verified on later examples.
priceIntro: Estimated retail values in U.S. dollars, as of October 2026. Condition and originality affect the final value.

sections.heading: Condition And Originality
sections.html: Bracing, herringbone trim, neck width, original finish and surviving top material determine the appropriate value range. A scalloped-braced 1944 guitar belongs in a different range from a non-scalloped example. Replacement tops, refinishing and major structural repairs need individual assessment. Confirm the wood on late-1969 guitars.

priceFootnote: The range depends on condition and originality. Dealer purchase offers and consignment proceeds differ from retail value.

description: Martin D-45 values for the 1968 and 1969 revival, with separate assessment of prewar guitars, restoration and provenance.
lede: A Brazilian-rosewood Martin D-45 from 1968 or 1969 is approximately $43,500 to $60,900, depending on condition and originality. Original prewar D-45s require individual appraisal.
scope: Original prewar D-45s and the 1968 to 1969 revival. Modern reissues, conversions and D-45S variants need separate comparisons.
priceIntro: Estimated retail values in U.S. dollars, as of October 2026. Condition and originality affect the final value.

sections.heading: Condition And Originality
sections.html: Original top, neck, finish, pearl work, bridge and bridge plate carry substantial weight. Extensive restoration can put a guitar below the stated range, while exceptional originals can exceed it. Factory D-45 identity, conversions and documented artist ownership need separate assessment.

priceFootnote: The range depends on condition and originality. Dealer purchase offers and consignment proceeds differ from retail value.

title: Early Martin Guitar Value Guide: Before 1920
description: Pre-1920 Martin guitar values for selected 2 1/2, 2, 1, 0 and 00 models, with notes on originality and condition.
lede: Early Martin values depend on body size, style, wood and condition. These ranges cover selected original Martin guitars made before 1920, from small parlor models to early 0 and 00 sizes.
scope: Original Martin guitars made through 1919. The listed periods apply only to the early instruments shown below.
priceIntro: Approximate retail values in U.S. dollars, as of October 2026, for pre-1920 guitars in excellent original condition.
rows: Other Pre-1920 Styles, Pearl Models And Unusual Variants

sections.heading: Condition And Originality
sections.html: Confirm the body size, style, wood and production period before selecting a range. Original finish, top, bridge, tuners and surviving case affect value. Neck angle, repaired cracks and structural damage also matter. Many early Martins were built for gut strings; altered bracing or damage from excessive string tension requires separate assessment. Replacement tops, extensive refinishing and rare pearl-trimmed styles need individual appraisal.

priceFootnote: Ranges assume excellent original condition. Dealer purchase offers and consignment proceeds differ from retail value.

title: Vintage Martin Tenor Guitar Value Guide
description: Vintage Martin tenor guitar value ranges by model and period, with notes on condition, original parts and conversions.
lede: Many vintage Martin tenor guitars range from roughly $1,100 to $4,000, depending on the model and year. Rare variants and substantially altered instruments require individual appraisal.
scope: Vintage 0-, 2- and 5-size T models, including mahogany and rosewood versions. Plectrum guitars have their own guide.
priceIntro: Estimated retail values in U.S. dollars, as of October 2026. Condition and originality affect the final value.

sections.html: Confirm the original four-string neck, scale, bridge and tuner arrangement. Replacement necks and conversions affect value. The price of a six-string Martin with a similar model number does not establish tenor value. Original parts, neck angle, repaired cracks and a usable setup all matter.
